remediation.suggestion: Disclose the external browser requests, or provide an offline template that bundles p5.js and uses local or system fonts.

content.value_statement: Generative art projects can be hard to structure, tune, and make reproducible. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to create p5.js artwork with seeded variation and interactive controls.
actual_capabilities: Creates an algorithmic philosophy before writing the visual implementation.
Uses p5.js patterns for seeded randomness, noise fields, particles, and parameterized systems.
Builds a single interactive HTML artifact based on the included viewer template.
Adds seed navigation so users can reproduce or explore variations.
Defines UI controls for parameters such as counts, scales, colors, thresholds, and motion.
Includes a generator reference template with reusable p5.js structure and utility functions.
limitations: Generated artifacts depend on browser execution and may load p5.js and fonts from external CDNs.
The skill guides creation but does not independently judge artistic quality or originality.
Large particle systems or animations may need performance tuning for slower devices.
It is focused on p5.js browser artifacts, not native graphics tools or print production workflows.

use_cases.title: Prototype generative art concepts
use_cases.description: Turn a visual idea into a reproducible p5.js sketch with parameters and seed controls.

use_cases.title: Create interactive portfolio pieces
use_cases.description: Build a self-contained browser artwork that viewers can adjust, regenerate, and export as an image.

use_cases.title: Teach computational aesthetics
use_cases.description: Use the philosophy-first workflow to explain how rules, randomness, and emergence shape visual systems.

prompt_templates.title: Begin with a simple theme
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a complete artwork from one idea.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an algorithmic art piece about ocean currents. Include the philosophy, p5.js artifact, seed controls, and a few simple sliders.

prompt_templates.title: Request a specific system
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request with a desired generative technique.
prompt_templates.prompt: Make a p5.js generative artwork using particle trails in a noise field. Use reproducible seeds and interactive controls for density, speed, and color.

prompt_templates.title: Explore variations
prompt_templates.scenario: User wants a tunable piece with strong variation support.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an interactive generative artwork with seed navigation and three preset variations. Explain how each seed changes the visual character.

prompt_templates.title: Develop an advanced concept
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for a concept-driven artifact.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a gallery-quality p5.js artwork based on recursive growth and constrained chaos. Make the parameters meaningful, keep the artifact self-contained, and optimize animation performance.

output_examples.input: Create art inspired by wind moving through tall grass.
output_examples.output: A short philosophy about field motion, followed by an interactive browser artwork with flowing strands, seeded variation, density controls, and color tuning.

output_examples.input: Make a geometric piece with reproducible randomness.
output_examples.output: A p5.js artifact that renders structured geometry from a seed, includes previous and next seed buttons, and exposes sliders for scale, symmetry, and color balance.

output_examples.input: I want a calm animated particle system.
output_examples.output: An interactive animation with slow particle drift, controlled noise, reset and regenerate actions, and guidance for adjusting performance-sensitive parameters.

best_practices: Start with the artistic concept, then choose algorithms that express that concept.
Keep seeds and parameters visible so outputs can be reproduced and compared.
Test the artifact in a browser after generation to verify controls and performance.
anti_patterns: Do not copy an existing artist style or copyrighted visual work directly.
Do not create static images when the request needs an algorithmic system.
Do not remove the required seed controls or replace the template with unrelated layout code.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates concept-driven p5.js generative art with seeded randomness, interactive controls, and a self-contained HTML artifact.

faq.question: Can I reproduce the same artwork later?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill requires seeded randomness so the same seed and parameters should produce the same result.

faq.question: Does it require a server?
faq.answer: No. The intended output is a single HTML artifact that can run in a browser or Claude artifact view.

faq.question: Can it make animated art?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports static or animated p5.js sketches, depending on the concept and performance needs.

faq.question: Can I change colors and parameters?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill asks for UI controls that match the generated artwork, including sliders and optional color pickers.

faq.question: What should I review before publishing an artifact?
faq.answer: Review external CDN use, browser performance, originality, and whether every control works as described.
